title: Watchtower: one Slack alert the moment an automation breaks
summary: Our own monitoring product for automation stacks. It watches n8n, GoHighLevel, Supabase and Vercel, posts one Slack alert per incident, and remembers how every error was fixed.
problem: Automations fail quietly. A broken workflow can drop leads for days before anyone notices, alerts flood channels with repeats, two people chase the same error, and the fix is forgotten by the next time it happens.
overview: Watchtower watches n8n, GoHighLevel, Supabase and Vercel and posts a single Slack alert when something fails. Repeats update the same message, and when someone resolves an error they write one line on what fixed it, so next time the alert already has the answer. We run it on every system we look after.

built.title: One alert per incident
built.detail: One Slack message with the workflow, the failing step and the error. Repeats update the original with a count instead of posting again.

built.title: Acknowledge
built.detail: Whoever picks up an error taps Acknowledge and the alert shows who has it, so nobody doubles up.

built.title: Resolve with the fix
built.detail: Resolving asks for a one-line note on what fixed it. When the same error returns, the alert shows the previous fix.

built.title: Open in n8n
built.detail: Every alert links straight to the failed execution, so the fix starts on the exact run that broke.

built.title: Watches four systems
built.detail: n8n errors are caught by an error workflow; GoHighLevel, Supabase and Vercel report in through a webhook, normalised into one format.

built.title: Supabase as memory
built.detail: Decides whether an error is new or a repeat, stores the Slack message for each incident and keeps the history of fixes.

built.title: Buttons on Vercel
built.detail: Every button press goes to a Vercel endpoint that updates Supabase and rewrites the Slack message.

built.title: Heartbeat collector
built.detail: Every inbound event bumps a heartbeat, so silence is noticed too: a feed that stops sending is as visible as one that errors.
